```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The 90-day goal is one paying customer, not scale. B's buyers are developers and platform leads who can buy self-serve on a card. Multiple live competitors publish self-serve tiers in the $19-199/mo range (Agentshield $49, OpenGuardrails $19/$99, SealGate up to $199), which shows a low-friction purchase path exists.",
    "B has a sourced near-zero-cash acquisition channel: a Show HN or open-source launch, backed by a cited launch guide. A's no-spend channel, parenting communities, is marked [unsourced cost], with reach and conversion described as unproven. A's only sourced channel is paid UA at $2.50-$5.00 CPI against a sub-$15/mo price, which the brief itself calls hard to justify for a solo operator.",
    "A has a sourced, mandatory pre-launch obligation: COPPA verifiable parental consent, cited to the FTC. It must be correctly implemented before collecting any child data, which eats into the build window. B's SOC 2 burden applies mainly to enterprise procurement, and per its own brief self-serve tiers are already being sold.",
    "B's demand evidence is a documented, cited incident (an agent deleting a production database and its backups) plus two cited developer quotes describing the exact control features the product would provide. A's demand quotes describe general frustration with teaching reading. The strongest one shows a parent declining to pay, which signals price sensitivity rather than a willingness to buy.",
    "A faces a free, well-resourced incumbent (Khan Academy Kids, cited as 100% free) that caps prices for undifferentiated offerings. Its brief offers no concrete differentiator, listing the niche as an open question.",
    "B has serious weaknesses that keep this from being a clear win. It has nine-plus competitors, several with free or OSS tiers, so willingness to pay is unproven. Its claim that buyers expect SOC 2 and EU AI Act evidence packs carries no citation. And trust in a one-person vendor sitting in the production execution path is a real barrier."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's organic parenting-community channel (r/daddit, r/homeschool, r/Parenting) is explicitly marked [unsourced cost], with reach and conversion called unproven. This is the channel A's Case For depends on to avoid paid UA that its own sourced CPI figures make uneconomic at a ~$15/mo price. Without it, A has no evidenced affordable path to a first paying customer.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe crowded markets with free alternatives, and neither presents evidence of someone actually paying a new entrant. B wins mainly on a cited self-serve buyer path and a sourced zero-cost launch channel, and on avoiding A's sourced COPPA pre-launch requirement. Its own differentiation and trust problems are significant, and its SOC 2 expectation claim is unsourced and could not be verified either way."
}
```
